# dsh-mermaid-renderer
English | 中文
A DeepSeek Harness (dsh) chat-UI plugin that renders **Mermaid code blocks** in the chat as diagram

cards.
Supports `flowchart / graph / sequenceDiagram / classDiagram / stateDiagram / erDiagram / jou
rney / gantt / pie / mindmap / timeline / C4Context / gitGraph` and more.
> **Works in both the command-line web UI and the official desktop app** — the desktop app embeds th

e same
> chat UI, and both hosts share one plugin codebase.

## Uninstall
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Desktop app: remove `dsh-mermaid-renderer` from the in-app Plugins page. Manual installs: delete the
`node_modules/dsh-mermaid-renderer/` directory and the bundles entry in the corresponding profile.
Restart the host afterwards.
## Compatibility & dependencies
- Browser half: no third-party runtime packages (hand-written static bundle in the official `dsh.cli

ent` /
`__ModuleLoader__` protocol); the inlined Mermaid engine ships with the file, so **no interne

t is required**;
- Host half: empty `apply` (present in the Cordis composition only), same pattern a

s the official `dsh-client-ui-*` packages;
- Manifest declares `dsh.client.immediately` and `inject:

["@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-conversation"]`, so the
plugin activates after the conversation UI is

d order** (fetched on the first diagram, then cached):
1. `window.__DSH_MERMAID_URL__` (custom mirro

r, settable from the console)
2. jsDelivr → unpkg (online, 8-second timeout, falls through on failur

e)
3. **the inlined engine** (ships inside `client.js` — the offline fallback)
- `lib/client.js` is

**generated** (≈3.43 MB with the engine inlined). Edit `lib/client.src.js` instead, then run
`node s
cripts/build-client.mjs`. Verify freshness with `node scripts/build-client.mjs --check`, and verify

the
engine with `node scripts/test-inline-engine.mjs`.
### Is that 3.43 MB downloaded repeatedly?
No. The host serves a plugin bundle with `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and b

undle URLs
carry a content fingerprint — so **nothing is re-transferred unless the plugin is upgrade

d**, the cache is
cleared, or the browser changes. In the desktop app the bundle is a local junction

to the source directory and
never crosses the network at all.
> Note: plugin bundles sit in the boot manifest's `application` preload batch, which is independent

of
> `dsh.client.immediately` — that flag governs *when the factory executes*, not *when the bytes a

re fetched*.
> See the corresponding section in `CHANGELOG.md`.
## Share / publish to the community
Distribution is GitHub-first (`main` branch + version tags + Releases). A publish script is included

, and it
takes the release notes **from the CHANGELOG section**, so the two never drift apart:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
> The script derives owner/repo from `git remote get-url origin` (so it works from a fork) and reads

the token
> from the git credential helper without printing it.
Other optional steps:
1. Upgrade the engine: re-run `scripts/vendor-mermaid.mjs` to refresh `.vendor/mermaid.min.js`, rebu
To offer a tarball for the desktop plugin manager's URL form, attach `npm pack` output to the Relea

to add an entry)
- awesome-dsh-plugins
- awesome-deepseek-harness
- Anil-matcha/awesome-dsh-plugin
> Optional: `npm publish` would also allow installing by package name. Not published at this time.
## How it works
The package is a standard dual-face dsh plugin: `cordis.patch.yml` (`dsh.bundle.patch`) inserts one
row (its `name` is the package name) into the profile composition; the host's client-modules service
(`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-modules`) discovers the `dsh.client` declaration, serves `lib/client.js`
through the plugins route and injects it into the boot manifest; the browser Cordis loader instantia
tes it and calls `apply(ctx)`. `apply` watches the chat DOM with a `MutationObserver`, lazy-loads Me
rmaid and renders SVG in place.
Styles, timers and DOM listeners are registered inside `apply`'s `ctx.effect`, so unloading the plug

in disposes
all of them and leaves no residue on the page.
> Why DOM post-processing instead of an official slot: the host currently exposes **no extension poi

nt for code
> block content** (none of the available slots can take over markdown code rendering, an

d the renderer package
> exposes no markdown/remark extension). The documented `conversation.chat.no

de` slot **adds** message rows and
> cannot rewrite existing code blocks. See the "known deviations"
section in `CHANGELOG.md`.
